title: ‘Less than a minute’: Hong Kong travellers praise Japan’s new tax refund at airports - South China Morning Post

‘Less than a minute’: Hong Kong travellers praise Japan’s new tax refund at airports | South China Morning Post Society - Society ‘Less than a minute’: Hong Kong travellers praise Japan’s new tax refund at airports Advertisement Hong Kong economy Hong Kong Society ‘Less than a minute’: Hong Kong travellers praise Japan’s new tax refund at airports 
 Visitors now pay 10 per cent consumption tax either at self-service airport kiosks or via Visit Japan Web instead of upfront at cash register
 2 -MIN READ 2 -MIN Listen Danny Mok and Eric Jiang Published: 10:43pm, 1 Nov 2026 Updated: 12:27am, 2 Nov 2026 Hong Kong tour groups returning from Japan have praised a smooth roll-out of the country’s new tax refund arrangement that requires travellers to complete refund procedures at airports or ports rather than at shops.
 Under the “pay first, refund later” scheme, which took effect on Sunday to curb illicit domestic reselling and tax evasion, international tourists must now pay the 10 per cent consumption tax upfront at the counter.
 Travellers are now required to complete customs verification before checking in their luggage, either at self-service airport kiosks or via the website Visit Japan Web. After verification, most will be cleared automatically, while some may be selected for customs inspection and asked to present their purchases.
